questions.q: How far behind time was Phileas Fogg at the start of the chapter?
choices: Eight hours
Twenty hours
Two full days
Eleven hours
questions.evidence: Phileas Fogg found himself twenty hours behind time.

questions.q: How did Passepartout feel about the delay?
choices: Desperate, because he believed he had ruined his master
Calm, because he trusted Fogg to find another train
Cheerful, because he was glad to be rescued alive
Angry, because he blamed Fix and the conductor for the delay

questions.q: What way of travelling did Fix suggest to Mr. Fogg?
choices: A sledge with sails
A team of fast horses
A boat down the Platte
A special hired train

questions.q: Who was the man who had spoken to Fix during the night?
choices: A soldier from the fort asking about the prisoners
Mudge, the owner of the sailing sledge
The conductor, asking him to board the train
A telegraph clerk with news from Omaha
questions.evidence: It was the man who had spoken to Fix during the night, and whose offer he had refused.

questions.q: The sledge was "rigged like a sloop." What does this tell you about it?
choices: It was pulled by a team of dogs
It had a mast and sails like a small boat
It ran along on steel railroad tracks
It was built mainly to carry heavy freight
questions.evidence: It was, in short, a sledge rigged like a sloop.

questions.q: What did Aouda decide when Mr. Fogg offered to leave her at Fort Kearney?
choices: She agreed to go to Europe later with Passepartout
She refused to be separated from Mr. Fogg
She asked to stay and care for the wounded
She said she would take the next train east
questions.evidence: Aouda refused to separate from Mr. Fogg

questions.q: What did Fix resolve to do, even if his opinion of Fogg had changed a little?
choices: Give up the case and travel home to Liverpool alone
Do his duty and hurry the whole party back to England
Tell Aouda the whole truth about the bank robbery
Leave the party at Omaha and wait for new orders
questions.evidence: he was nevertheless resolved to do his duty

questions.q: What were the two things Phileas Fogg had to fear on the sledge trip?
choices: Wolves, and a frozen river breaking under them
An accident to the sledge, and a change or calm in the wind
Getting lost in the snow, and running short of food
Sioux riders, and a heavy snowstorm from the north
questions.evidence: an accident to the sledge, and a change or calm in the wind

questions.q: What did Mr. Fogg say about the sounds made by the singing lashings?
choices: "Those chords give the fifth and the octave."
"That noise will surely frighten off the wolves."
"The mast will break if this wind keeps on."
"We are going faster than any express train."
questions.evidence: Those chords give the fifth and the octave

questions.q: What did Passepartout feel he would never forget?
choices: The day the sledge flew over the frozen Platte
The sacrifice Mr. Fogg made to rescue him
The cold that made his face as red as the sun
The kindness of the soldiers at Fort Kearney
questions.evidence: the sacrifice which Mr. Fogg had made, without hesitation, to rescue him from the Sioux

questions.q: What animals chased the sledge across the plain?
choices: Buffalo
Prairie-wolves
Wild horses
Black bears
questions.evidence: bands of gaunt, famished, ferocious prairie-wolves ran howling after the sledge

questions.q: What did the party do as soon as they reached the Omaha station?
choices: Rested for a night at a hotel in Omaha
Jumped onto a train that was ready to start
Telegraphed New York to hold the steamer
Walked around the snowy town to see the sights
questions.evidence: they only had time to get into the cars

questions.q: What disappointing news ends the chapter?
choices: The train for New York has been cancelled for the night
The China for Liverpool left three-quarters of an hour before
Fix has telegraphed the police to wait for them at the New York pier
The Hudson River is frozen and no boat can cross it
questions.evidence: The China, for Liverpool, had started three-quarters of an hour before!
